problem: Queryable-map ObjectNav methods (VLFM, OneMap, ZSON) ground targets with text-only queries, which become unreliable for fine-grained or product-level subcategories (e.g. 'IKEA Markus chair'). Existing benchmarks also lack a long-tail, subcategory-level ObjectNav evaluation.
motivation: Web image search offers abundant visual examples even for rare categories, and humans consult images to identify unfamiliar objects, yet retrieval has not been integrated into embodied navigation as a plug-and-play mechanism. Text alone gives insufficient visual cues as semantic specificity increases, so visual examples should improve map grounding.
key_idea: Retrieve N web images for the target query, encode them with the map's VLM, match each against the semantic map, and average the similarity maps (optionally with the text map) for zero-shot, plug-and-play localization.
insight: Image-conditioned queries consistently improve grounding, and image-only is about as good as image+text, so the retrieved visual context is the dominant signal. Arithmetic-mean aggregation is far better than harmonic mean or hybrid (e.g. SigLIP OVON-syn 29.35 vs 4.19 harmonic). End-to-end gains on the long-tail set are modest because detection is the bottleneck: failure analysis shows mis-detection at 29.8%, and conditioning YOLOWorld on retrieved images lifts OneMap SR on HSSD-rare from 7.05 to 11.75.
method: Web-image retrieval: fetches top-n images (n=10 for OVON-syn, 15 for HSSD-rare) using the head category prepended to the query, filters by ALT-text/URL head-noun gating, deduplicates and caches them, at ~0.61 s per image
Queryable semantic map: VLFM-style 2D grid map of VLM features (BLIP2 holistic or SED patch embeddings) projected via depth, with averaging over repeated observations
Image-conditioned querying: encodes the retrieved images, computes one cosine similarity map per image, and averages them, optionally adding the text similarity map
Static phase: target-free frontier exploration (3000 steps, 4 m depth mask and range, dropping patches at depth discontinuities) builds a fixed map to evaluate grounding in isolation
Online phase: plugs the image-conditioned similarity maps into the VLFM/OneMap/ZSON loop while leaving the policy and detector unchanged
IMPRINT* detector variant: conditions YOLOWorld in OneMap on the top-3 retrieved reference images
HSSD-rare benchmark: 1000 episodes, 17 HSSD scenes, 20 main categories, 559 subcategories, with a custom viewpoint-generation pipeline using ray-cast boundaries and depth-based visibility checks

setting.backbone: BLIP2 (VLFM), SED (OneMap), CLIP-based policy (ZSON), SigLIP in the static study; all frozen, with YOLOWorld as detector
setting.training_data: none (training-free, zero-shot; web images retrieved at test time)
setting.action_space: discrete actions with frontier-based exploration and a PointGoal controller
setting.privileged: none at test time; web image retrieval is an external resource. The static phase uses a pre-explored map for grounding evaluation only.

numbers.extra: web images retrieved at test time; SR at 1 m

numbers.backbone: SED + YOLOWorld with top-3 reference images
SED + YOLOWorld with top-3 reference images

numbers_note: OVON-syn is val_seen_synonyms; OVON split names are not mapped precisely to the canonical val labels. HSSD-rare is the paper's new benchmark, and no official split is given so 'test' is a placeholder. Static-phase results for BLIP2 and SigLIP are also in the paper but not listed here.
results: IMPRINT improves grounding for all encoders on both datasets, with average static SR gains of +10.54 on OVON-syn and +6.37 on HSSD-rare. Online, it raises VLFM SR from 23.83 to 27.17 on OVON-syn and from 12.74 to 13.91 on HSSD-rare, with smaller gains for OneMap and ZSON. Conditioning the detector on retrieved images (IMPRINT*) raises OneMap HSSD-rare SR to 11.75 from 7.05.
limitations: Depends on relevant web images being available for rare categories, and online navigation gains are small on the long-tail set because of detector bottlenecks
HSSD-rare is synthetic and small (17 scenes), so it may not reflect real-world long-tail navigation
Real-world validation is minimal (5 episodes), and absolute SRs remain low
compares_to: text-only queries with BLIP2, SigLIP and SED
